summary: The paper completely resolves both open questions posed by Sun regarding unary-tracked unitary synthesis and Wide Fredkin decompositions. It proves universal T-count lower bounds showing that unary tracker updates require at least K_j non-Clifford gates (refuting poly(n) updates) and that m-pair Wide Fredkin gates require at least 2m + 1 T-gates (refuting sublinear o(m) decompositions). It introduces optimal symplectic-Gram factorizations achieving 4m + 3 T-gates for Wide Fredkin, subspace-optimal routing achieving 8K_j and 4K_j T-gates, and eliminates sawtooth ancilla inflation in QSD space-depth volume laws. All mathematical claims are formally verified in Lean 4 and checked via exact Q(zeta_8) cyclotomic arithmetic.
strengths: Definitive resolution of both open questions from Sun [1] with matching asymptotic and exact lower bounds.
Comprehensive formal verification in Lean 4.35.0 (15/15 theorems, zero sorry, zero axioms) and exact Q(zeta_8) cyclotomic verification (16/16 SHA-256 certificates).
Novel symplectic-Gram matrix factorization approach providing an optimal 4m + 3 ancilla-free circuit for Wide Fredkin gates.
Rigorous treatment of stabilizer-nullity monotonicity under adaptive circuits with measurements and ancillas.
weaknesses: Highly specialized domain requiring advanced quantum circuit synthesis and stabilizer formalism background.
